name: Sé Catedral de Nossa Senhora da Graça
region: São Tomé · São Tomé and Príncipe
subtitle: Historic cathedral and seat of one of the earliest Catholic dioceses established in sub-Saharan Africa (1534).

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Reconstructed in late 19th-century Portuguese revival style with twin bell towers

facts.label: Setting
facts.value: Praça do Povo in downtown São Tomé

parts.text: The main cathedral and bishop's seat of the Diocese of São Tomé and Príncipe, situated on Praça do Povo in the historic heart of the capital. Originally founded in the early 16th century, its episcopal see was elevated in 1534, making it one of the most venerable Catholic diocesan seats across sub-Saharan Africa. Rebuilt and renovated across the centuries, its current facade combines Portuguese colonial baroque and neoclassical elements, featuring dual bell towers and blue-and-white azulejo tile decorations.

gaps: Parish archive records prior to the late 19th-century renovation are partially preserved.
